"* The article is an interview with a famous writer named Jeffrey Eugenides. He recently published a new book of short stories. In one of his stories, he wrote that learning about your country is like learning about yourself, because both can make you feel ashamed. He believes that personal problems and national problems are deeply connected. When a nation has problems, it is basically just a reflection of the people living in it. You might feel a lot of tension when you watch the news today. Sometimes, people argue about politics with a friend or a girlfriend. These intense arguments can even affect a person's mental health. The writer wants to highlight how we all have things in our past that we are not proud of. Coping with this reality is something every citizen has to do in their daily life.
* The interview takes place in a library at Princeton University, where the author works as a teacher. The building they are in is so new that it is not even completely finished yet. There is a simple paper sign on the bathroom door that says it is for any gender, which shows how much society has changed recently. This change is a welcome update for many people on college campuses. When he toured for his most famous book, Middlesex, back in 2003, people did not know much about gender differences. He often had to explain to people what the word intersex actually meant. Today, people are much more aware of these kinds of topics. The author points out that our society is constantly changing and evolving. We are learning to accept each other more over time. By simply talking about these issues, he helps us understand the world better."
